facts.text: Reverend Ben Deering named the settlement “Webb Chapel,” laid out the town, and set aside a whole block for a Methodist church and school.
The Louis and San Francisco Railroad arrived in Webb City in 1879, followed by the Missouri Pacific in 1881, marking the town’s first rail connections.
After discovering lead in 1873, Webb leased his land to the Center Creek Mining Company, which began operations in 1876 and sparked the town’s mining boom.
The Webb City Public Library’s third floor hosts a genealogy room where visitors can view old newspapers and an 1877 stereoview of the mining company.
John C. Webb platted the town on a 200‑acre farm he entered in 1857, later leasing the land to mining companies that drove Webb City’s early growth.
